title: How to Use Less Mobile Data on Android
html:
Start by finding out where your data goes. Settings shows mobile data use per app. Once you know the top apps, set a warning so the number does not surprise you, turn on Data Saver, and change the three settings that use data without you noticing: app updates, photo backup and video quality.

Last updated: 10 Oct 2026. The paths below are from Google's Pixel help; other brands use similar menus with different names, so use the Settings search box.

I checked the Data usage screens on a vivo V23 Pro running Android 14 (Funtouch OS 14, security update January 2025) on 10 Oct 2026. Sections 1 to 5 follow Google's Pixel help and the menus are not all the same on my phone; the path on my phone is in section 6.

1. See which apps use your data

Open Settings, then Network and internet, then SIMs, then App data usage. You can change the time period with the drop-down. Look at the top three or four apps and ask whether that matches how much you use them.

2. Set a warning, and a limit if you want one

Go to Settings, then Network and internet, then SIMs, then Data warning and limit. Turn on "Set data warning" and enter an amount. You get a notification when you reach it. If you turn on "Set data limit" instead, Google says mobile data switches off automatically when you hit the limit, and you get a notification.

Note that the phone counts data in its own way. Your operator's count is the one that matters for your plan, so check the two against each other for a few days.

3. Turn on Data Saver

Open Settings, then Network and internet, then Data Saver. Google says that with this mode on, most apps and services get background data only over Wi-Fi, while the apps you are using right now can still use mobile data. If an app you need stops updating in the background, go to Data Saver, then Unrestricted data, and allow that app.

4. Update apps on Wi-Fi only

In the Play Store, tap your profile picture, then Settings, then Network preferences, then Auto-update apps. The options are: update over Wi-Fi or mobile data, update with a limited amount of mobile data, update over Wi-Fi only, or do not auto-update. Pick "Update over Wi-Fi only".

5. Photo backup and video quality

  • Google Photos: tap your profile picture, then Photos settings, then Backup, then Mobile data usage. You can set a daily limit for automatic backup and turn off "Back up videos over data".
  • YouTube: tap your profile picture, then Settings, then Video quality preferences. "Data saver" gives lower picture quality, but videos may start faster. For downloads, use "Download over Wi-Fi only" under Background and downloads.

6. Other things that use data

Google also lists turning off auto-sync (you then sync by hand) and switching mobile data off completely to use Wi-Fi only. Data roaming has its own switch under Network and internet, then SIMs.

On my vivo V23 Pro the path is Settings, then Network and internet, then SIM card and mobile network, then SIM card info and settings, then Data usage. Tap an app in the list and its page splits the month into Foreground and Background, and has a Background data switch and an Unrestricted data usage switch (the second one only matters when Data Saver is on). For Instagram on my phone the month showed 16.86 GB in total: 16.30 GB in the foreground and only 578 MB in the background. So for that app, turning off background data would not have saved much. Most of the data went while I was using it. I did not turn the switch off, so I cannot say what it does to notifications.

If an app uses a lot of data and battery while you are not using it, our guide to battery drain shows how to limit it.

What to do next

  1. Open App data usage and note the top apps.
  2. Set a data warning.
  3. Turn on Data Saver and allow only the apps that need background data.
  4. Set app updates to Wi-Fi only, and check Google Photos and YouTube.
